title: Paul before the Sanhedrin + the plot to kill him and the transfer to Caesarea

paragraphs.text: And Paul, looking stedfastly on the council, said, Brethren, I have lived before God in all good conscience until this day.
paragraphs.original: ἀτενίσας δὲ ὁ Παῦλος τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ θεῷ ἄχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας.
paragraphs.translit: atenisas de ho Paulos tō synedriō eipen· Andres adelphoi, egō pasē syneidēsei agathē pepoliteumai tō theō achri tautēs tēs hēmeras.

paragraphs.text: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας ἐπέταξεν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν αὐτῷ τύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de archiereus Hananias epetaxen tois parestōsin autō typtein autou to stoma.

paragraphs.text: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: and sittest thou to judge me according to the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
paragraphs.original: τότε ὁ Παῦλος πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Τύπτειν σε μέλλει ὁ θεός, τοῖχε κεκονιαμένε· καὶ σὺ κάθῃ κρίνων με κατὰ τὸν νόμον, καὶ παρανομῶν κελεύεις με τύπτεσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: tote ho Paulos pros auton eipen· Typtein se mellei ho theos, toiche kekoniamene· kai sy kathē krinōn me kata ton nomon, kai paranomōn keleueis me typtesthai;

paragraphs.text: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God`s high priest?
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ παρεστῶτες εἶπαν· Τὸν ἀρχιερέα τοῦ θεοῦ λοιδορεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: hoi de parestōtes eipan· Ton archierea tou theou loidoreis;

paragraphs.text: And Paul said, I knew not, brethren, that he was high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of a ruler of thy people.
paragraphs.original: ἔφη τε ὁ Παῦλος· Οὐκ ᾔδειν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀρχιερεύς· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἄρχοντα τοῦ λαοῦ σου οὐκ ἐρεῖς κακῶς.
paragraphs.translit: ephē te ho Paulos· Ouk ēdein, adelphoi, hoti estin archiereus· gegraptai gar hoti Archonta tou laou sou ouk ereis kakōs.

paragraphs.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees: touching the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
paragraphs.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ὅτι τὸ ἓν μέρος ἐστὶν Σαδδουκαίων τὸ δὲ ἕτερον Φαρισαίων ἔκραζεν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ Φαρισαῖός εἰμι, υἱὸς Φαρισαίων· περὶ ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι.
paragraphs.translit: Gnous de ho Paulos hoti to hen meros estin Saddoukaiōn to de heteron Pharisaiōn ekrazen en tō synedriō· Andres adelphoi, egō Pharisaios eimi, hyios Pharisaiōn· peri elpidos kai anastaseōs nekrōn egō krinomai.

paragraphs.text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and Sadducees; and the assembly was divided.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐγένετο στάσις τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων, καὶ ἐσχίσθη τὸ πλῆθος.
paragraphs.translit: touto de autou lalountos egeneto stasis tōn Pharisaiōn kai Saddoukaiōn, kai eschisthē to plēthos.

paragraphs.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess both.
paragraphs.original: Σαδδουκαῖοι μὲν γὰρ λέγουσιν μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν μήτε ἄγγελον μήτε πνεῦμα, Φαρισαῖοι δὲ ὁμολογοῦσιν τὰ ἀμφότερα.
paragraphs.translit: Saddoukaioi men gar legousin mē einai anastasin mēte angelon mēte pneuma, Pharisaioi de homologousin ta amphotera.

paragraphs.text: And there arose a great clamor: and some of the scribes of the Pharisees part stood up, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: and what if a spirit hath spoken to him, or an angel?
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ κραυγὴ μεγάλη, καὶ ἀναστάντες τινὲς τῶν γραμματέων τοῦ μέρους τῶν Φαρισαίων διεμάχοντο λέγοντες· Οὐδὲν κακὸν εὑρίσκομεν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ· εἰ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ἢ ἄγγελος—
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de kraugē megalē, kai anastantes tines tōn grammateōn tou merous tōn Pharisaiōn diemachonto legontes· Ouden kakon heuriskomen en tō anthrōpō toutō· ei de pneuma elalēsen autō ē angelos—

paragraphs.text: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the castle.
paragraphs.original: πολλῆς δὲ γινομένης στάσεως φοβηθεὶς ὁ χιλίαρχος μὴ διασπασθῇ ὁ Παῦλος ὑπʼ αὐτῶν ἐκέλευσεν τὸ στράτευμα καταβὰν ἁρπάσαι αὐτὸν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, ἄγειν τε εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.
paragraphs.translit: pollēs de ginomenēs staseōs phobētheis ho chiliarchos mē diaspasthē ho Paulos hypʼ autōn ekeleusen to strateuma kataban harpasai auton ek mesou autōn, agein te eis tēn parembolēn.

paragraphs.text: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer: for as thou hast testified concerning me at Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
paragraphs.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ νυκτὶ ἐπιστὰς αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος εἶπεν· Θάρσει, ὡς γὰρ διεμαρτύρω τὰ περὶ ἐμοῦ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ οὕτω σε δεῖ καὶ εἰς Ῥώμην μαρτυρῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Tē de epiousē nykti epistas autō ho kyrios eipen· Tharsei, hōs gar diemartyrō ta peri emou eis Ierousalēm houtō se dei kai eis Rhōmēn martyrēsai.

paragraphs.text: And when it was day, the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
paragraphs.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ποιήσαντες συστροφὴν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸν Παῦλον.
paragraphs.translit: Genomenēs de hēmeras poiēsantes systrophēn hoi Ioudaioi anethematisan heautous legontes mēte phagein mēte piein heōs hou apokteinōsin ton Paulon.

paragraphs.text: And they were more than forty that made this conspiracy.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ πλείους τεσσεράκοντα οἱ ταύτην τὴν συνωμοσίαν ποιησάμενοι·
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de pleious tesserakonta hoi tautēn tēn synōmosian poiēsamenoi·

paragraphs.text: And they came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες προσελθόντες τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις εἶπαν· Ἀναθέματι ἀνεθεματίσαμεν ἑαυτοὺς μηδενὸς γεύσασθαι ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωμεν τὸν Παῦλον.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines proselthontes tois archiereusin kai tois presbyterois eipan· Anathemati anethematisamen heautous mēdenos geusasthai heōs hou apokteinōmen ton Paulon.

paragraphs.text: Now therefore do ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you, as though ye would judge of his case more exactly: and we, before he comes near, are ready to slay him.
paragraphs.original: νῦν οὖν ὑμεῖς ἐμφανίσατε τῷ χιλιάρχῳ σὺν τῷ συνεδρίῳ ὅπως καταγάγῃ αὐτὸν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὡς μέλλοντας διαγινώσκειν ἀκριβέστερον τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ· ἡμεῖς δὲ πρὸ τοῦ ἐγγίσαι αὐτὸν ἕτοιμοί ἐσμεν τοῦ ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: nyn oun hymeis emphanisate tō chiliarchō syn tō synedriō hopōs katagagē auton eis hymas hōs mellontas diaginōskein akribesteron ta peri autou· hēmeis de pro tou engisai auton hetoimoi esmen tou anelein auton.

paragraphs.text: But Paul`s sister`s son heard of their lying in wait, and he came and entered into the castle and told Paul.
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀδελφῆς Παύλου τὴν ἐνέδραν παραγενόμενος καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ Παύλῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Akousas de ho hyios tēs adelphēs Paulou tēn enedran paragenomenos kai eiselthōn eis tēn parembolēn apēngeilen tō Paulō.

paragraphs.text: And Paul called unto him one of the centurions, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain; for he hath something to tell him.
paragraphs.original: προσκαλεσάμενος δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἕνα τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν ἔφη· Τὸν νεανίαν τοῦτον ἄπαγε πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον, ἔχει γὰρ ἀπαγγεῖλαί τι αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: proskalesamenos de ho Paulos hena tōn hekatontarchōn ephē· Ton neanian touton apage pros ton chiliarchon, echei gar apangeilai ti autō.

paragraphs.text: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and saith, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and asked me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say to thee.
paragraphs.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν παραλαβὼν αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ φησίν· Ὁ δέσμιος Παῦλος προσκαλεσάμενός με ἠρώτησεν τοῦτον τὸν νεανίαν ἀγαγεῖν πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντά τι λαλῆσαί σοι.
paragraphs.translit: ho men oun paralabōn auton ēgagen pros ton chiliarchon kai phēsin· Ho desmios Paulos proskalesamenos me ērōtēsen touton ton neanian agagein pros se, echonta ti lalēsai soi.

paragraphs.text: And the chief captain took him by the hand, and going aside asked him privately, What is it that thou hast to tell me?
paragraphs.original: ἐπιλαβόμενος δὲ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ ἀναχωρήσας κατʼ ἰδίαν ἐπυνθάνετο· Τί ἐστιν ὃ ἔχεις ἀπαγγεῖλαί μοι;
paragraphs.translit: epilabomenos de tēs cheiros autou ho chiliarchos kai anachōrēsas katʼ idian epynthaneto· Ti estin ho echeis apangeilai moi;

paragraphs.text: And he said, The Jews have agreed to ask thee to bring down Paul tomorrow unto the council, as though thou wouldest inquire somewhat more exactly concerning him.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὅτι Οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέθεντο τοῦ ἐρωτῆσαί σε ὅπως αὔριον τὸν Παῦλον καταγάγῃς εἰς τὸ συνέδριον ὡς μέλλον τι ἀκριβέστερον πυνθάνεσθαι περὶ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de hoti Hoi Ioudaioi synethento tou erōtēsai se hopōs aurion ton Paulon katagagēs eis to synedrion hōs mellon ti akribesteron pynthanesthai peri autou·

paragraphs.text: Do not thou therefore yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who have bound themselves under a curse, neither to eat nor to drink till they have slain him: and now are they ready, looking for the promise from thee.
paragraphs.original: σὺ οὖν μὴ πεισθῇς αὐτοῖς, ἐνεδρεύουσιν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες πλείους τεσσεράκοντα, οἵτινες ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, καὶ νῦν εἰσιν ἕτοιμοι προσδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἐπαγγελίαν.
paragraphs.translit: sy oun mē peisthēs autois, enedreuousin gar auton ex autōn andres pleious tesserakonta, hoitines anethematisan heautous mēte phagein mēte piein heōs hou anelōsin auton, kai nyn eisin hetoimoi prosdechomenoi tēn apo sou epangelian.

paragraphs.text: So the chief captain let the young man go, charging him, Tell no man that thou hast signified these things to me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν χιλίαρχος ἀπέλυσε τὸν νεανίσκον παραγγείλας μηδενὶ ἐκλαλῆσαι ὅτι ταῦτα ἐνεφάνισας πρὸς ἐμέ.
paragraphs.translit: ho men oun chiliarchos apelyse ton neaniskon parangeilas mēdeni eklalēsai hoti tauta enephanisas pros eme.

paragraphs.text: And he called unto him two of the centurions, and said, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενός τινας δύο τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν εἶπεν· Ἑτοιμάσατε στρατιώτας διακοσίους ὅπως πορευθῶσιν ἕως Καισαρείας, καὶ ἱππεῖς ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ δεξιολάβους διακοσίους, ἀπὸ τρίτης ὥρας τῆς νυκτός,
paragraphs.translit: Kai proskalesamenos tinas dyo tōn hekatontarchōn eipen· Hetoimasate stratiōtas diakosious hopōs poreuthōsin heōs Kaisareias, kai hippeis hebdomēkonta kai dexiolabous diakosious, apo tritēs hōras tēs nyktos,

paragraphs.text: and [he bade them] provide beasts, that they might set Paul thereon, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
paragraphs.original: κτήνη τε παραστῆσαι ἵνα ἐπιβιβάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον διασώσωσι πρὸς Φήλικα τὸν ἡγεμόνα,
paragraphs.translit: ktēnē te parastēsai hina epibibasantes ton Paulon diasōsōsi pros Phēlika ton hēgemona,

paragraphs.text: And he wrote a letter after this form:
paragraphs.original: γράψας ἐπιστολὴν ἔχουσαν τὸν τύπον τοῦτον·
paragraphs.translit: grapsas epistolēn echousan ton typon touton·

paragraphs.text: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.
paragraphs.original: Κλαύδιος Λυσίας τῷ κρατίστῳ ἡγεμόνι Φήλικι χαίρειν.
paragraphs.translit: Klaudios Lysias tō kratistō hēgemoni Phēliki chairein.

paragraphs.text: This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be slain of them, when I came upon them with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
paragraphs.original: τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον συλλημφθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ μέλλοντα ἀναιρεῖσθαι ὑπʼ αὐτῶν ἐπιστὰς σὺν τῷ στρατεύματι ἐξειλάμην, μαθὼν ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: ton andra touton syllēmphthenta hypo tōn Ioudaiōn kai mellonta anaireisthai hypʼ autōn epistas syn tō strateumati exeilamēn, mathōn hoti Rhōmaios estin,

paragraphs.text: And desiring to know the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him down unto their council:
paragraphs.original: βουλόμενός τε ἐπιγνῶναι τὴν αἰτίαν διʼ ἣν ἐνεκάλουν αὐτῷ, κατήγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: boulomenos te epignōnai tēn aitian diʼ hēn enekaloun autō, katēgagon eis to synedrion autōn.

paragraphs.text: whom I found to be accused about questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
paragraphs.original: ὃν εὗρον ἐγκαλούμενον περὶ ζητημάτων τοῦ νόμου αὐτῶν, μηδὲν δὲ ἄξιον θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἔχοντα ἔγκλημα.
paragraphs.translit: hon heuron enkaloumenon peri zētēmatōn tou nomou autōn, mēden de axion thanatou ē desmōn echonta enklēma.

paragraphs.text: And when it was shown to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to thee forthwith, charging his accusers also to speak against him before thee.
paragraphs.original: μηνυθείσης δέ μοι ἐπιβουλῆς εἰς τὸν ἄνδρα ἔσεσθαι ἐξαυτῆς ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, παραγγείλας καὶ τοῖς κατηγόροις λέγειν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ σοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mēnytheisēs de moi epiboulēs eis ton andra esesthai exautēs epempsa pros se, parangeilas kai tois katēgorois legein pros auton epi sou.

paragraphs.text: So the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται κατὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον αὐτοῖς ἀναλαβόντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον διὰ νυκτὸς εἰς τὴν Ἀντιπατρίδα·
paragraphs.translit: Hoi men oun stratiōtai kata to diatetagmenon autois analabontes ton Paulon ēgagon dia nyktos eis tēn Antipatrida·

paragraphs.text: But on the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
paragraphs.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐάσαντες τοὺς ἱππεῖς ἀπέρχεσθαι σὺν αὐτῷ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν·
paragraphs.translit: tē de epaurion easantes tous hippeis aperchesthai syn autō hypestrepsan eis tēn parembolēn·

paragraphs.text: and they, when they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν καὶ ἀναδόντες τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τῷ ἡγεμόνι παρέστησαν καὶ τὸν Παῦλον αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines eiselthontes eis tēn Kaisareian kai anadontes tēn epistolēn tō hēgemoni parestēsan kai ton Paulon autō.

paragraphs.text: And when he had read it, he asked of what province he was; and when he understood that he was of Cilicia,
paragraphs.original: ἀναγνοὺς δὲ καὶ ἐπερωτήσας ἐκ ποίας ἐπαρχείας ἐστὶν καὶ πυθόμενος ὅτι ἀπὸ Κιλικίας,
paragraphs.translit: anagnous de kai eperōtēsas ek poias eparcheias estin kai pythomenos hoti apo Kilikias,

paragraphs.text: I will hear thee fully, said he, when thine accusers also are come: and he commanded him to be kept in Herod`s palace.
paragraphs.original: Διακούσομαί σου, ἔφη, ὅταν καὶ οἱ κατήγοροί σου παραγένωνται· κελεύσας ἐν τῷ πραιτωρίῳ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Diakousomai sou, ephē, hotan kai hoi katēgoroi sou paragenōntai· keleusas en tō praitōriō tou Hērōdou phylassesthai auton.
